From: Samir Patel <samir@medicore.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-15 09:12 AM -0700
Subject: Renewal quote feedback / account at risk

Olga,

Thanks for the renewal packet. After reviewing the numbers with procurement and product, Medicore cannot accept the proposed increase — the new per-token rates and the reduced SLA credits will put our costs >35% higher. Our execs are pressuring us to consolidate with a cheaper provider unless there is flexibility on pricing and a short-term SLA add-on while we finish a migration PoC.

We value the platform and the performance, but this renewal as quoted will force us to evaluate alternatives. Can you escalate for any short-term concessions (one-time credit, term reset to 12 months with a step-down rate, and an SLA credit during the transition)? Procurement is standing by.

– Samir
Director of Cloud Ops
Medicore Health

Appreciate the candid note. I’ve looped in Vivek (SVP Sales) and Deal Desk to escalate. We absolutely want to avoid you moving during a migration window.

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-15 10:22 AM -0700
Subject: Escalation: Medicore renewal — exec approval request

Team —

Escalating MED-8472 (Medicore Health). They are evaluating alternatives due to a ~35% cost increase under our renewal quote. Key facts:
- ARR at renewal: ~$1.1M; strong product usage (embeddings + generation), steady QPS.
- Renewal term proposed: 24 months at published volumes and new price tier.
- Customer asks: one-time retention credit, term reset to 12 months, and an SLA uplift (or an SLA-specific credit window) for a 90-day migration buffer.

Proposed concession package for approval (to retain account):
1) One-time credit = 18% of first-year ARR (applied as invoice credit).
2) Term reset to 12 months with step-down pricing at month 7 (10% off list for months 7–12 if usage thresholds met).
3) Temporary SLA overlay: 99.95% SLA for the renewal quarter with a 2% service credit cap for verified incidents during the first 90 days.
4) Waive onboarding fee and include a complementary 3 months of priority support (no additional charge).

Attachments: Medicore_SOW_v3.pdf, license_rationale.xlsx (cost impact and legal redline). Numbers in license_rationale.xlsx show the net NPV impact ≈ -12% first-year revenue vs quoted full term but preserves renewal and upsell motion.

Request: Exec approval to offer the above concessions. If approved, I’ll share the package with procurement and send an updated Quote + DocuSign.

Thanks,
Olga

Olga/Ben —

Reviewed the ask and the numbers. High-level guidance: retention here is strategically important (healthcare reference customer, impressive usage, future procurement opportunity). I approve a constrained concession set with these guardrails: 
- Authorize one-time credit up to 20% of first-year ARR but require signoff by Finance on net revenue recognition.
- Term reset to 12 months is acceptable but we should include a performance breakpoint (usage thresholds) for any additional step-down discounts.
- SLA overlay for 90 days is OK, but cap the service credit at 2% and require operational runbook + incident SLA obligations documented in the SOW.

Ben — please validate final pricing math and confirm approval if the NPV delta is <= -15% for year one (post-credit). If Finance requires, escalate to CFO.

If Ben confirms, Olga — proceed to present to Medicore and ask for procurement contact to sign updated doc.

— Vivek
SVP Sales, Redwood Inference
